race:human.title: Humans
race:human.summary: Short-lived, stubborn and everywhere. Humans rebuilt the world after the Breaking faster than anyone thought possible, and have been arguing about who owns it ever since.

sections.title: Who they are
sections.text: Humans live about seventy years, which the elves find tragic and the humans find motivating. They are the most numerous people of Valdren, and the only one with towns on every road. What they lack in years they make up in ambition: a human who wants something will usually die trying, and frequently gets it first.

sections.title: Where they live
sections.text: The heartland of humanity is what remains of the old realm of Aster: the knightly [[culture:human.crownlands|Crownlands]], the merchant city of [[culture:human.freeport|Freeport]] and the frontier passes of the [[culture:human.highmarch|Highmarch]]. Free towns like [[place:lanternford|Lanternford]] sit between them and belong to everyone.

sections.title: History
sections.text: Humans call the Sundering the Breaking, and remember it as the time their scattered villages first had to band together or die. Out of that came the realm of Aster and the [[era:banners|Age of Banners]], and the Banner Wars that ended it. The [[era:hungry-years|Hungry Years]] are still within living memory.

sections.title: Among the Pact
sections.text: Brannoc Vale of the [[era:first-five|First Five]] was a human knight, and humans still make up the largest share of the [[faction:pact|Pact]]. They are good at everything and best at nothing, the old joke goes, which is exactly what a band needs when someone has fallen.

facts: Versatile: 5% more XP from every battle
quote: We do not have the years. So we have the nerve.

heritage:human.title: Human Heritage
heritage:human.summary: Human heritage is what families and towns pass down: a trade, a name, a grudge, a song. Renown among humans comes from deeds told in taverns, and grows fastest when kin fight side by side.

sections.title: Sagas at the bar
sections.text: Humans have no great book of history. They have taverns. Every deed a human hero does gets told at a bar somewhere, and the telling is what makes it last. That is Renown: being worth retelling. A human who rides with other humans gets retold more, because there is always someone at the table who was there.

heritage:human.trunk0.title: Ambition
heritage:human.trunk0.summary: The human hunger to be more than you were born to. Humans never stop learning, because they never have enough time.

heritage:human.trunk1.title: Many Hands
heritage:human.trunk1.summary: Humans built the realm of Aster by sharing work out. A human with many friends is strong in many ways at once.

heritage:human.trunk2.title: Sagas
heritage:human.trunk2.summary: The deeds told about you at the bars of every town. The more you are retold, the more Renown each run brings.

heritage:human.crownlands0.title: Drilled
heritage:human.crownlands0.summary: The drill-yards of the Crownlands, where squires learn to hold a line until holding it is easier than breaking.

heritage:human.crownlands1.title: Courtly Grace
heritage:human.crownlands1.summary: The manners of Asterhold's court. A knight who can bow well can usually also stand well.

heritage:human.crownlands2.title: Crownlands Kinship
heritage:human.crownlands2.summary: Knights of the Crownlands call each other shield-brothers and shield-sisters, and fight harder when one of them is beside them.

heritage:human.freeport0.title: Haggler
heritage:human.freeport0.summary: Freeport children learn to bargain before they learn to read. Gold seems to find them.

heritage:human.freeport1.title: Sea Legs
heritage:human.freeport1.summary: The balance of someone who grew up on a rolling deck, where every step is a dodge.

heritage:human.freeport2.title: Freeport Kinship
heritage:human.freeport2.summary: The crew is blood in Freeport. Two Freeporters in a band trust each other the way only smugglers can.

heritage:human.highmarch0.title: Frontier Born
heritage:human.highmarch0.summary: Highmarch winters kill the weak. Those born there are hard to knock down and quick to get up.

heritage:human.highmarch1.title: Pathfinder
heritage:human.highmarch1.summary: The wardens of the passes know every trail, every ambush spot, and exactly where to strike.

heritage:human.highmarch2.title: Highmarch Kinship
heritage:human.highmarch2.summary: The watchtowers of the Highmarch are held by families. A Highmarcher fights for the one next to them as for their own tower.

culture:human.crownlands.title: Crownlands
culture:human.crownlands.kicker: Knights and banners of the old kingdom
culture:human.crownlands.summary: The rolling green heartland of the old realm of Aster, ruled from Asterhold. Castles on every hill, chapels in every village, and a knightly house behind every old grudge.

sections.title: The land
sections.text: Wheat fields, orchards and slow rivers, broken up by castles and walled towns. The Crownlands fed the realm of Aster in its glory and fed half the world during the [[era:hungry-years|Hungry Years]], and they have never let anyone forget it.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Crownlanders love order: ranks, titles, banners, the right way to pour wine. Knightly houses train squires in castle yards, Lantern chapels ring the hours, and every family can name the house it served in the Banner Wars. They are proud, sometimes too proud, and loyal to the bone.

sections.title: Asterhold
sections.text: The capital, seat of the [[faction:crown|Crown]], built on a hill over the sealed [[hollow:cinder-gate|Cinder Gate]]. Its palace cellars are the most guarded room in the world.

facts: A hand on the heart and a small bow
quote: A knight is a promise that walks.

culture:human.freeport.title: Freeport
culture:human.freeport.summary: The great free harbour city of the Saltreach coast. Everything in the world passes through its docks, and something is skimmed off all of it.

sections.title: The city
sections.text: Freeport broke away from Aster in the Banner Wars and never looked back. Its harbour is a forest of masts, its streets smell of tar, fish and money, and its laws are set by the [[faction:syndics|Syndics]], who are merchants, and enforced by the watch, who are paid by merchants.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Freeporters bargain about everything, trust their crew completely and nobody else at all, and consider smuggling a respectable family trade. They are generous to friends, sharp with strangers, and the first to sell grain to anyone in trouble, at a fair price, for Freeport.

sections.title: The sea
sections.text: Freeport ships sail the Saltreach and beyond. The sea gives and takes: there are few Freeport families without a name in the harbour chapel's book of the lost.

facts: Trade, ships, smugglers, the Quiet Hand's first house
What's the news, and what's it worth?
quote: Everything has a price. Most things have two.

culture:human.highmarch.title: Highmarch
culture:human.highmarch.kicker: Frontier wardens of the mountain passes
culture:human.highmarch.summary: The hard country of the Greyteeth passes, held by watchtower families against raiders, trolls and whatever comes down from the snow.

sections.title: The land
sections.text: Steep valleys, goat trails and stone villages clinging to the slopes of the [[place:greyteeth|Greyteeth]]. Every pass has a watchtower, and every watchtower has been held by the same family for longer than anyone can remember.

sections.title: The people
sections.text: Highmarchers are quiet, practical and very hard to kill. They take the name warden from the old order of the wild, though most of them guard passes rather than forests. They trust the mountain, their neighbours and very little else, and they share everything in winter because winter does not care who you are.

sections.title: Dangers
sections.text: Raiders in summer, [[beast:trolls|trolls]] in winter, avalanches in spring. The Highmarch has lost whole villages in the worst years, and rebuilt every one of them.

facts: A nod. Two if they like you.
quote: The mountain keeps no grudges. Neither should you. But keep your boots dry.

backstory:human.squire.title: Squire of the Crown
backstory:human.squire.summary: Raised in a castle yard of the Crownlands, among squires who polish armour, carry lances and wait for knights to come home.

sections.title: The yard
sections.text: Every great house of the [[culture:human.crownlands|Crownlands]] keeps a castle yard full of squires: children of minor families, sent to learn arms and manners. Many of the knights they served rode out in the last hard years and never came back. The squires kept polishing the armour anyway.

backstory:human.courtier.title: Fallen Courtier
backstory:human.courtier.summary: Once a voice at the court of Asterhold, until a scandal, a debt or a wrong word struck their name from the heralds' lists.

sections.title: The court
sections.text: The court of the [[faction:crown|Crown]] runs on whispers, favours and seating plans. A courtier who falls from it keeps the manners and loses everything else, and usually knows far too much about who owes whom.

backstory:human.bannerchild.title: Child of the Banner
backstory:human.bannerchild.summary: Born in a war camp of the Crown and raised by the whole company, from the cook to the captain.

sections.title: The company
sections.text: The Crownlands companies still march to the border every summer. Children born on the march belong to everyone, and grow up knowing how to pitch a tent, mend a strap and sleep through a drum.

backstory:human.dockhand.title: Dockhand
backstory:human.dockhand.summary: Grew up on the Freeport wharf, hauling crates and haggling for every copper the Syndics did not already own.

sections.title: The wharf
sections.text: The docks of [[culture:human.freeport|Freeport]] never sleep. Dockhands learn which crates are heavy because they are full and which are heavy because they are hiding something, and they learn not to ask which.

backstory:human.deckhand.title: Ship's Boy
backstory:human.deckhand.summary: Ran away to sea at nine and learned to fight, climb and swear on a rolling deck.

sections.title: The sea
sections.text: Freeport ships always need small hands for the rigging. The sea teaches balance, nerve and how to keep your footing when everything moves, which turns out to be useful in a [[world:hollows|Hollow]].

backstory:human.crewborn.title: Crew-born
backstory:human.crewborn.summary: One of the old Freeport smuggling families, where the crew is blood and the family business is never written down.

sections.title: The families
sections.text: The smuggling families of [[culture:human.freeport|Freeport]] are older than the [[faction:syndics|Syndics]] and prouder. They have no seats on the council, but the council does not move a ship without asking them.

backstory:human.shepherd.title: Mountain Shepherd
backstory:human.shepherd.summary: Kept a flock alive through Highmarch winters that killed whole villages.

sections.title: Winter
sections.text: In the [[culture:human.highmarch|Highmarch]], shepherding is a war against the cold. A shepherd who brings the flock down in spring with no losses is talked about in every village of the pass.

backstory:human.scout.title: Pass Scout
backstory:human.scout.summary: Walked the high trails ahead of the wardens, watching for raiders, trolls and the first signs of a Hollow.

sections.title: Ahead of everyone
sections.text: Pass scouts go where the wardens will go tomorrow. They were the first to see the warm cracks and fleeing goats that mean a [[world:hollows|Hollow]] is coming, and the [[faction:pact|Pact]] pays well for their reports.

backstory:human.wardenkin.title: Warden's Kin
backstory:human.wardenkin.summary: Every generation of the family has held the same watchtower in the Highmarch.

sections.title: The tower
sections.text: Highmarch watchtowers pass from parent to child, along with a horn, a ledger and a list of the dead. Leaving the tower to walk with the [[faction:pact|Pact]] is allowed, but the tower expects you back.

answer:human.grandparents.0.summary: The knights of the old realm rode out under Aster's silver star in the Banner Wars. Many families still hang a helm over the hearth for one who never came home.

answer:human.grandparents.1.summary: During the Hungry Years the farms that held on fed whole valleys, and their families are honoured at every market.

answer:human.grandparents.2.summary: Freeport's harbour chapel keeps a book of the lost. Sailors who never come back are written there, and their logbooks are read aloud on Lantern Night.

answer:human.grandparents.3.summary: Hedge-wizards work small magic without the towers' training. Lantern priests distrust them; everyone with a fever goes to them anyway.

answer:human.parents.0.summary: Crossroads inns are where news travels in the human lands. Many also keep a small tavern board for the Pact.

answer:human.parents.1.summary: Minor lords of the Crown keep stewards to count their grain and guard captains to protect it, and the two rarely agree.

answer:human.parents.2.summary: Peddlers carry goods and gossip between the villages the big merchants ignore, and know every road from Freeport to the passes.

answer:human.parents.3.summary: The Lantern chapels have run orphanages since the Hungry Years, and are known for teaching discipline before letters.

answer:human.siblings.0.summary: Big families are the human answer to short lives: more hands for the farm, more voices at the table, and someone always on your side in a fight.

answer:human.siblings.1.summary: Lantern priests say twins share one light split in two, and that each will always know when the other is in danger.

answer:human.siblings.2.summary: Only children are rare in the human lands, and are often sent to the chapel schools, where the books outnumber the children.

answer:human.siblings.3.summary: After the Hungry Years, half the families of the Crownlands took in an orphaned cousin. Nobody remembers it as charity; it was just what you did.

answer:human.birth.0.summary: Comets are read as signs by every faith. The Lantern priests argue whether they are sparks of the first flame or warnings from the deep.

answer:human.birth.1.summary: After the grey summers of the Hungry Years, every good harvest since is celebrated as if it might be the last.

answer:human.birth.2.summary: Town fires are common where a Hollow is near; the ground warms, the wells run hot, and one dry night everything goes up.

answer:human.birth.3.summary: King Aldric's procession travels the realm each spring. Families who see it pass on the day of a birth name the child after one of his knights, for luck.

answer:human.friend.0.summary: Stablehands are the best-informed people in any town: everyone who arrives or leaves does it on a horse.

answer:human.friend.1.summary: Three-legged dogs are oddly common in the Highmarch, where trolls and traps take a leg and the dog keeps going anyway.

answer:human.friend.2.summary: Freeport merchant heirs are sent inland to learn the trade roads, and usually learn a great deal more than their parents wanted.

answer:human.friend.3.summary: Human towns run on rivalries: mill against mill, street against street. The best friendships start with a race nobody agrees on.

answer:human.play.0.summary: Every Crownlands child plays at knights. The real tournaments at Asterhold are held each midsummer, and the pot-lid champions are always watching.

answer:human.play.1.summary: Market days bring peddlers, Freeport spices, dwarf tools and elf silver to even the smallest town.

answer:human.play.2.summary: Lantern chapel choirs sing the hours so the lamp never goes out in silence. Stealing a candle is a sin, but a small and very common one.

answer:human.play.3.summary: Town walls in the human lands were built for the Banner Wars, and have been climbed by children ever since.

answer:human.teen.0.summary: Old knights of the Crown take squires long after their own riding days are over, and teach what the drill-yard cannot.

answer:human.teen.1.summary: Every city has its street gangs. The best of them end up in the Quiet Hand, and the rest end up in the stocks.

answer:human.teen.2.summary: Human scholars copy the old books of Aster by hand, and pay their apprentices in the only coin they have.

answer:human.teen.3.summary: Farm work in the Crownlands is dawn to dusk from sowing to harvest. Knights recruit from the fields for a reason.

answer:human.firstfight.0.summary: The Pact asks every hero one question when they swear: would you stand up for a stranger? Most first fights answer it before anyone asks.

answer:human.firstfight.1.summary: Duels over insults are banned in the Crownlands and happen every week anyway, at dawn, behind the chapel.

answer:human.firstfight.2.summary: Sellswords drift through every town since the Banner Wars ended. Talking one down takes more nerve than fighting.

answer:human.firstfight.3.summary: The north road out of the Crownlands has had bandits on it for as long as it has had travellers.

answer:human.mentor.0.summary: Retired sergeants of the Crown's companies drill the town youth in the square each morning, partly for the realm and mostly for something to do.

answer:human.mentor.1.summary: Village priests of the Lantern Faith teach that every light can be rekindled, even one that has gone very dim.

answer:human.mentor.2.summary: Travelling bards carry the sagas from tavern to tavern. Without them nobody would know the First Five's names.

answer:human.mentor.3.summary: Highmarchers say the mountain is the oldest teacher and the hardest, and that its lessons are the only ones that stick.

answer:human.leaving.0.summary: The Pact is the surest way for a human to make a name: a deed told at the Five Flagons travels faster than any herald.

answer:human.leaving.1.summary: The trade guilds of Freeport do not forgive debts, but they do accept treasure from a Hollow.

answer:human.leaving.2.summary: When the muster bells ring, the Pact calls every hero to a Hollow too large for one band.

answer:human.leaving.3.summary: Most bands of the Pact began as two friends on a road. The other three join later.

answer:human.deed.0.summary: Bridges are where Hollows spill over. Every bridge in Lanternford has been held by someone, and rebuilt after.

answer:human.deed.1.summary: The harvest games are held across the Crownlands each autumn, and a commoner who beats a lord's huntsman is remembered for life.

answer:human.deed.2.summary: The Greywater runs cold from the Highmarch down through Lanternford, and its bridges are the pride of the towns that build them.

answer:human.deed.3.summary: Freeport respects nothing more than a fortune made from nothing, and asks no questions about how.

answer:human.loss.0.summary: Hollow fevers come up with the heat of a Hollow and burn through towns nearby. Even Lantern clerics cannot always break them.

answer:human.loss.1.summary: Since the Banner Wars, minor lords seize land on old claims nobody can disprove. The Crown rarely takes the side of the farmer.

answer:human.loss.2.summary: Human lives are short, and human loves are often shorter. The bards have a song for every kind.

answer:human.loss.3.summary: The Pact says the dark takes something from everyone eventually. It also says a band is how you carry the loss when it comes.

answer:human.fear.0.summary: To be told at the bar is to live on. The Pact carves the names of the fallen into the floor of the Five Flagons so nobody is forgotten.

answer:human.fear.1.summary: Humans say a temper runs in the blood like a river runs downhill, and that only a good friend can dam it.

answer:human.fear.2.summary: Every band of the Pact depends on everyone. The oath's second rule, hold the line for each other, is the one heroes lose sleep over.

answer:human.fear.3.summary: The Greywater runs fast and cold. Every human child of Lanternford is told a river story, and most of them are true.

answer:human.keepsake.0.summary: Signet rings of minor houses carry crests that were once on Aster's banners. Most are worth more as memory than as gold.

answer:human.keepsake.1.summary: Unsent letters are common among Pact heroes. Some leave them with the keepers of the Five Flagons, to be sent if they do not come back.

answer:human.keepsake.2.summary: A whetstone handed down is a Highmarch tradition: three generations of blades kept sharp for the same tower.

answer:human.keepsake.3.summary: Meadow flowers are pressed into books across the Crownlands as tokens of home. Their colours fade; the habit never does.

answer:human.drive.0.summary: A family name can be won back in the Pact. The Five Flagons has seen many a disgraced house restored by a single deed in a Hollow.

answer:human.drive.1.summary: Since the Banner Wars, land in the Crownlands is bought rather than given. Hollow treasure has paid for more farms than any lord.

answer:human.drive.2.summary: Human maps end at the Ashlands, the dunes and the far sea. The Waking has started putting new Hollows past every edge.

answer:human.drive.3.summary: The Pact asks nothing of its heroes but the four rules, and justice is not one of them. Humans tend to add it anyway.
